summary: Verified that /index-standalone.html correctly posts a `phone` field (not `email`) to the Google Apps Script webhook. Intercepted outbound POSTs via Playwright page.on('request') for both Hyderabad (pincode 500034) and non-Hyderabad (pincode 560001) submissions. All 22 payload assertions passed. Our client-side code is doing its job correctly — the bug is on the user's Apps Script side (still referencing d.email).
action_items: No changes needed on our side. Confirm to user that the deployed standalone HTML sends `phone` in the JSON body. User must update their Apps Script to read d.phone instead of d.email and redeploy (New deployment) for the change to take effect.
critical_code_review_comments: index-standalone.html payload correctly includes: id, name, phone, address, pincode, baby_name, baby_age, is_hyderabad, created_at. No `email` key is sent.

fetch uses mode:'no-cors' with Content-Type 'text/plain;charset=utf-8' — this is standard for Apps Script Web Apps to avoid CORS preflight while still delivering the body. Apps Script's doPost receives it via e.postData.contents.
Consider adding data-testid attributes to form inputs (#f-name, #f-phone, #f-pincode, #submit-btn, #success) for future automated testing robustness — currently only #id selectors are available.
seed_data_creation: None. Two test submissions were sent (fire-and-forget, mode:'no-cors') to the Apps Script webhook using unique phones 9876543211 (Hyderabad) and 9123456780 (Bengaluru). These may appear as rows in the linked Google Sheet if the Apps Script writes them.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Standalone HTML lives at /app/frontend/public/index-standalone.html. Public URL: {REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/index-standalone.html. The waitlist form fires a no-cors POST to window.MUMZO_SHEETS_URL (Google Apps Script). The payload uses `phone` (10-digit) — NOT `email`. HYD pincode regex is /^(500|501)\d{3}$/. Non-Hyd submissions fill address/baby_name/baby_age with the em-dash character '—'.
rca of the issue: User reported phone not saving to Google Sheet from deployed Hostinger site. RCA: user's Apps Script code still references d.email from the previous schema, while our frontend now sends d.phone. Verified via network interception that our HTML sends `phone` correctly in both HYD and non-HYD flows. Mitigation: user must edit Apps Script (doPost) to use d.phone and redeploy as a new version (Apps Script Web Apps require a new deployment for changes to be picked up).
